business_problem: Lifespan needed to make surgical consent forms easier for patients to understand because the documents were still written at a college reading level and could undermine health literacy during emotionally difficult care decisions.
solution_summary: Lifespan built a tightly governed document-simplification workflow around GPT-4 to rewrite surgical consent forms into plain language without changing meaning. Medical residents first identified that consent forms remained too complex for many patients, then used a simple prompt to ask GPT-4 to preserve content while rewriting the text to the average American reading level. The model produced an initial draft at roughly a sixth-grade reading level, after which legal and medical reviewers checked the output to mitigate hallucination and bias before deployment. That human-in-the-loop flow let Lifespan move from dense three-page documents toward simpler one-page forms, then extend the same process to other clinical paperwork such as intake and chemotherapy consent forms. The result is an implementation that keeps AI as the first-pass drafting layer while clinicians and legal staff remain the final authority on what reaches patients.

solution_components.name: GPT-4
solution_components.role: Creates the first simplified draft of surgical consent forms while preserving their original meaning.

data_flow: Lifespan feeds an existing surgical consent form and a simplification prompt into GPT-4, receives a plain-language draft, routes that draft through legal and medical review, and then deploys the approved version across the health system as patient-facing documentation.
business_outcome: Lifespan made consent forms more accessible for patients, reduced document length and complexity, and created a repeatable AI-assisted workflow for simplifying other forms across the health system.
